chapter: Kenton, Granz, Parker and the jazz clubs
title: First jazz clubs played
summary: He lists jazz rooms: Ebony Club, Royal Roost, Bop City, Birdland, and clubs in several cities.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Was the -- was the Carnegie Hall concert the first one where you played in concert Midtown?
Well, you played Midtown in club conditions, right?
Well, you played -- you played in clubs ever since '41, right, in --
I play all around (inaudible), and I played a whole lot of jazz rooms.
(Inaudible) Room we played -- we played the BLYEDLAND --
Then we opened at B OP City. When the B OP City opened, we was the first group there.
(Inaudible) we played the BIRDLAND. But the first club, the first jazz club -- Dicky Wells (inaudible) opened there. What was the name? The Ebony Club.
Ebony Club. This was Dicky Wells, the trombonist.
No, no. A guy that used to have a club uptown. He used to go with Talullah Bankhead, all that.
So you opened at the Ebony Club.

That's -- I think that was the first jazz club we played. (Inaudible) and we went to the Royal Roost, Royal Roost over there between 47 and 48th. And then I remember the Royal Roost -- I don't know whether it was B OP City opened or Birdland (inaudible), but we play around there. And then we went to Philadelphia to play the Holland Club in Philadelphia. We play another club on the West Side. We played the -- another gas club that used to be in Broad Street (inaudible).
Then we went to High Hat in Boston. We played Rhode Island, another gas club. We went to the Blue Moon, Chicago.
We played (inaudible) in California. We played at (inaudible) in San Francisco. We played all the jazz room band --
